transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you that brought you in today?

Well, I'm here because everybody keeps acting like I'm just imagining things. But I know for a fact my wife's relative has been coming into my house to get at me. 

Look, I work with my hands all day, I know exactly where I leave my things. My tools don't just move themselves. And it's not just the tools. Every weekend, my fishing plans get spoiled, and it's no accident. It's been going on for months now, and... well, I can see it plain as day. He's been trying to take over my place and push me right out of my own home. I'm just tired of people telling me it's not happening when it's right there in front of me.
Do you believe that others are trying to harm you or take something from you, even if there's no clear proof?

Like I was just saying, it's not that there's no proof. The proof is right in front of everyone, but everybody keeps acting like I'm just imagining it. 

So, yes, he is trying to take something from me. My wife's relative is trying to take my home. He's coming into the house to get at me, messing with the tools on my workbench, ruining my fishing trips every single weekend... it's all so he can push me out and take over my place. I don't just believe it, I know it's happening, even if nobody else wants to look at the facts.
Do you ever see, hear, or feel things that others don’t seem to notice, even when you’re sure they’re really there?

No, nothing like that. I mean... I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, if that's what you're asking. I'm not crazy. I just see what's actually happening in my own house, like the tools being moved. But no, I don't see or hear anything unusual like that.
Do you feel like you are being targeted or singled out by others in situations beyond your home, like at work or in public places?

No, not really. I mean... work is fine. I just go in, do my job, and come home. Nobody at the shop is messing with me or anything. And out in public... no, people just mind their own business. 

It's really just my house. That's where the problem is. It's just him, my wife's relative, doing all this to me. I don't have any issues with anyone else out in town or at work.
Can you explain how you know it’s specifically your wife’s relative doing this, and have you ever considered that someone else might be responsible or that there could be another explanation?

Well... who else would it be? I mean, I’m here talking to you right now because everybody keeps acting like I’m just imagining it, but there is no other explanation. I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. 

It's just common sense. My tools out on the workbench... they don’t just move themselves. And my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every single weekend. It's too calculated. After all these months of this happening, I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. So no, I haven't considered anyone else, because all the facts point right to him.
Have you ever confronted your wife's relative about moving your tools or ruining your fishing plans?

No, I haven't. I mean, there's really no point in confronting him directly. He's just going to lie and play dumb, isn't he? A guy who sneaks into another man's house to mess with his things isn't going to just admit it when you ask him. 

I've told my wife to keep him away, but... well, she just takes his side and tells me I'm making it up. So no, I haven't had it out with him face-to-face. It wouldn't do any good anyway.
Have you ever considered, even briefly, that your belief about your wife's relative might not be accurate, even if you can't see another explanation right now?

No. Not even for a minute. 

Like I was just saying a minute ago... I'm only here because everybody keeps acting like I'm imagining the whole thing. But I know he came into this house to get at me. I don't need to second-guess it because the proof is right there. My tools don't just pick themselves up and move around the bench. Every single weekend, my fishing plans get spoiled—that's not just some accident. 

After all these months of dealing with it, I can see plain as day that he's just trying to take over my place and push me out. So no, I haven't considered that I'm wrong about him, because I'm not.
Are there any other things you believe strongly that others don’t seem to understand or agree with, outside of what’s been happening in your home with your wife's relative?

No, I... no, nothing like that. I don't have any weird ideas about the world, if that's what you're asking. 

I'm just a regular guy. I go to the shop, do my job putting parts together, pay my bills, and try to mind my own business. There's nothing else going on. It's literally just this one situation with her relative messing with my house and my things. Outside of him, my life is completely normal. I just want the guy to leave me alone so I can live in peace.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs in the past that turned out not to be true, but you were absolutely sure about them at the time?

No, never. I've never had anything like that happen before. 

Like I said, I'm just a normal guy. I trust my own eyes and my own experiences. If something happens, it happens, and I deal with it. I don't go around making things up or imagining things that aren't there. Everything I've ever known to be true has been true. 

This whole thing with her relative... it's the only time I've ever had a problem like this, where I know exactly what's going on, but nobody else will listen to me. But no, I haven't had any other situations where I was wrong about something I was sure of.
Have you ever had any experiences where you strongly believed something was happening or was true, that others couldn’t confirm, even if it wasn’t related to your wife’s relative or your home?

No, I haven't. I... I feel like you're just asking me the same question again, doc. 

Like I said, there's nothing else. I don't have any other strange beliefs or experiences where people don't believe me. I don't think the government is after me or anything like that. It's literally just this one problem with her relative. Outside of what he's doing to my house, everything else in my life is just regular, everyday stuff. So no, nothing else.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that others couldn’t confirm, even if they seemed obvious to you, even if they weren’t related to your wife’s relative or your home?

Look, doc... I really don't know how many different ways I can say it. You are literally just asking me the exact same question again. 

No. I haven't. 

I don't have any other beliefs like that. I've never been in a situation where I knew something was true and nobody else could see it, except for this thing with my wife's relative. That is the only thing. Like I said, I just go to work, do my assembling, and come home. There's nothing else to tell you about. Can we please move on from this?
Have you ever had any other unshakable beliefs that others couldn’t confirm, even if they seemed completely obvious to you, even if they weren’t related to your wife’s relative or your home?

Doctor, I... I'm starting to get a little frustrated here. You've asked me this same thing four times now, just changing the words around a bit. 

The answer is still no. I don't have any other unshakable beliefs or whatever you want to call them. I'm a regular guy. I assemble parts for a living, I pay my bills, I mind my own business. There's nothing else going on with me. The only issue I have is the one we've been talking about, with her relative messing with my house. That's it. Nothing else.

inference_history.note: The patient presents with beliefs that others are deliberately acting against him (persecutory-type delusions), suggesting possible Delusional Disorder (F22) or Schizophreniform Disorder (F23.2). Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent, Severe (F33.3) is considered due to the patient's frustration and possible mood symptoms. Adjustment Disorder with Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood (F43.23) is also considered as a lower-severity explanation for the patient’s stress response to ongoing difficulties.

The patient denies perceptual disturbances such as hallucinations, which makes some psychotic disorders less likely, but does not eliminate them entirely given the presence of non-bizarre delusions. No new disorder has been added or ruled out definitively this turn.

The patient does not report any mood episodes, recurrent depressive episodes, or symptoms consistent with PTSD or prolonged grief. The delusional content appears non-bizarre, circumscribed, and fixed, without evidence of hallucinations, disorganized thinking, or prominent mood symptoms, which makes F22 (Delusional Disorder) more likely. F23.2 (Persistent Delusional Disorder) remains a candidate due to the chronic nature of the delusion (>months). F33.3 and F43.23 have been ruled out due to absence of mood and trauma-related features respectively.
